classification.difficultyReason: Convert compound units and currency using successive unitary steps, including an inverse conversion.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A large tank is leaking water at 20 mL per second. Express this rate in litres per hour.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Leak rate}&=\frac{20}{1000}\text{ L/s}\\\text{Leak rate}&=0.02\times60\text{ L/min}\\\text{Leak rate}&=1.2\times60\text{ L/h}\\\text{Leak rate}&=72\text{ L/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Every student in a school of 800 throws away an average of 200 g of rubbish a day. If there are 200 days in the school year, what is the rate at which the students throw away rubbish, in kilograms per year?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{School's daily rubbish}&=800\times200\text{ g/day}\\\text{School's daily rubbish}&=160\,000\text{ g/day}\\\text{School's daily rubbish}&=160\text{ kg/day}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{School's yearly rubbish}&=160\times200\text{ kg/year}\\\text{School's yearly rubbish}&=32\,000\text{ kg/year}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: The water stored in Warragamba Dam went from 41.6% of the dam’s capacity to 40.4% in a 30-day period. At what weekly rate, as a percentage of the dam’s total capacity, is the water being used?

answer.short: 0.28% of the dam’s total capacity per week.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Capacity used in 30 days}&=(41.6-40.4)\%\\\text{Capacity used in 30 days}&=1.2\%\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Daily use}&=\frac{1.2}{30}\%\\\text{Daily use}&=0.04\%\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Weekly use}&=7\times0.04\%\\\text{Weekly use}&=0.28\%\end{align*}$$
The stored water decreases by 0.28 percentage points of total capacity per week.

children.label: d
children.prompt: A car travels 100 km on 15 L of petrol. At what rate is the car using petrol, in units of kilometres per litre?

answer.worked:
15 L allows the car to travel 100 km.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance per litre}&=\frac{100}{15}\text{ km/L}\\\text{Distance per litre}&=\frac{20}{3}\text{ km/L}\\\text{Distance per litre}&=6\frac{2}{3}\text{ km/L}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: At a certain time, one Australian dollar bought 72 US cents.

answer.worked:
$\text{A}\$1$ buys $\text{US}\$0.72$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{US-dollar value of A}\$12&=12\times\$0.72\\\text{US-dollar value of A}\$12&=\$8.64\end{align*}$$

72 US cents buys $\text{A}\$1$, so 1 US cent buys $\text{A}\$\frac{1}{72}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Australian-dollar value of US}\$18&=\frac{1800}{72}\text{ Australian dollars}\\\text{Australian-dollar value of US}\$18&=\text{A}\$25\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: At a certain time, one Australian dollar bought 40 British pence. Express in Australian dollars the price of a jug that cost 55 British pounds. (There are 100 British pence in a British pound.)

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Jug price in British pence}&=55\times100\\\text{Jug price in British pence}&=5500\end{align*}$$
40 British pence buys $\text{A}\$1$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Jug price in Australian dollars}&=5500\div40\\\text{Jug price in Australian dollars}&=137.50\end{align*}$$
The jug costs $\text{A}\$137.50$.
